title: Apprenticeship (NAPS)
kicker: Vocational / Skilling · Earn while you train

value.body: An apprenticeship is paid, structured training at a real workplace — a factory, hospital, bank, retailer or service firm — under the Apprentices Act, 1961. The National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS), launched in 2016, encourages employers to take on apprentices by sharing part of the stipend. Training combines basic classroom learning with on-the-job work.

items.label: Government share of stipend
items.note: Paid to the apprentice by DBT; the employer pays the rest

items.label: Minimum monthly stipend
items.note: Depends on qualification; an upward revision was proposed in 2025

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Register on the national Apprenticeship India portal, browse openings by trade and location, and apply; the employer shortlists and signs an apprenticeship contract. Each trade sets its own minimum age and education. Class 12 pass students — as well as ITI and diploma holders — can apply for fresher and optional-trade apprenticeships.

value.title: At a glance
items: You earn a stipend while training — it is a stipend, not a salary.
Apprentices take an assessment at the end and receive a certificate; a permanent job with the same employer is not guaranteed.
Openings cluster in industrial states and cities, so relocation may be needed.
Graduates and diploma holders also have a parallel scheme, NATS, run by the Ministry of Education.
